changes.current_line: Customers see an average uplift in authorization rates with Authorization Boost and Adaptive Acceptance.
changes.change: Use this lead when a prospect brings a decline problem from their own dashboard: Stop losing the big baskets at the last step. We'll show you why your largest orders get declined, and what those failed orders are worth in your own numbers. Keep the average uplift claim as supporting proof under this lead. Do not open with it.
changes.why: The champion described her pain as "orders dying at the last step" on "the big baskets", while our "uplift slide" was what reached the CFO, and he read the switch as paying more for "the same thing".

changes.change: Add a standard offer for champions who have to sell internally to a finance decider we can't meet: a one-page business case built from a three-month export of their own declines. It shows how many orders failed, what they were worth, and what we expect to recover. Make the offer as soon as a champion asks for something to hand finance.
changes.why: Lucy asked for "something she could hand Martin" and got "the deck and the pricing proposal", although the SE had offered to show "what the failed orders were worth" and the CFO never met us.

changes.change: Add a counter for deals where an incumbent bank processor cuts its rate: the cost of staying. Give the champion our own side-by-side before their finance team builds theirs. It should show the full cost, not only the rate line, and the dollar value of the failed orders the current processor still can't explain.
changes.why: The bank responded with "Just a better rate" and the controller's one-pager compared only rates, so the failed-order value "wasn't on the page" and the conversation turned into "Can you do better on the rate".
